olivia: quick heads-up — the model-version comparison dashboard for /chat routing shows a token-level SLO drift on model-v2 canary vs model-v1 this morning. p50 +10ms, p95 +48ms. :eyes:
ryan: ugh. which breakdown is spiking? kernel selection, KV hits, or batching?
maria: looking at the token-latency waterfall panel now — kernel time is up for the last 30m on sequences >512. KV hitrate looks stable (~87%). batching efficiency down ~12% on canary nodes.
shahzad: can you paste the query you used for per-token breakdown? i want to cross-check with the profiler logs.
maria: sure — Grafana panel uses this prom query for token breakdown by stage:
```
sum by(stage,model_version)(rate(runtime_token_latency_seconds_sum[5m])) / sum by(stage,model_version)(rate(runtime_token_latency_seconds_count[5m]))
```
olivia: infra-monitor-bot posted an alert at 1866002100: `token_latency_sli{route="/chat",model_version="v2"} > 30ms` for 3m :warning:
infra-monitor-bot: alert auto-generated. current p95=48.2ms, threshold=40ms, affected nodes=canary-*-gpupool
ryan: curious if kernel picker fell back to a non-opt kernel under specific seq lengths. run profiler on one canary pod and check `kernel_choice` histogram.
maria: attached a snippet from the profiler (trimmed):
```
[2026-03-02T09:12:01Z] seq_len=768 model=v2 kernel_choice=quant_fast_cuda latency=1.8ms
[2026-03-02T09:12:02Z] seq_len=1024 model=v2 kernel_choice=fp16_generic latency=3.9ms  <-- spike
[2026-03-02T09:12:03Z] seq_len=256 model=v2 kernel_choice=quant_fast_cuda latency=0.9ms
```
shahzad: that fp16_generic line is a red flag — quant kernel should cover those seq lengths. maybe the kernel selector thresholds changed after the last rollout. did the kernel selector config get shipped with v2?
olivia: yes, v2 included a conservative kernel selector patch that widened the fallback window (to preserve compatibility with a new attention op). we thought perf impact would be negligible.
ryan: batching heuristic note: canary traffic has a slightly different seq_len distribution (more long-context tests). our continuous-batching accelerator opts for smaller batch size to meet latency SLOs which reduces batching efficiency. that + occasional kernel fallback would explain the p95 jump.
maria: i ran an A/B panel comparing route=/chat model=v1 vs v2 by token-stage, here's an export (summary):
- model-v1 p50 tokens: 12.3ms, kernel 4.1ms, kv 1.2ms, io 2.0ms
- model-v2 p50 tokens: 22.5ms, kernel 11.3ms, kv 1.1ms, io 2.0ms
- model-v2 p95 tokens: 48.2ms, (kernel contribution ~34ms)
olivia: that kernel contribution dominance is concerning. action items?
shahzad: short term: roll-forward a config revert to tighten kernel selector thresholds for canary nodes only. patch: `kernel_selector.fallback_threshold_seq_len=1024` -> 1400 (undo).
ryan: also propose increasing batching window by 5ms on canary to boost batching efficiency for long sequences, route-scoped: `batcher.max_wait_ms: 5`
maria: both changes sound good. perf team suggests instrumenting a new gauge `kernel_fallback_rate{model_version}` for the dashboard so we can correlate quickly next time.
olivia: agreed. i'll open a canary-only rollback patch and a follow-up perf instrumentation ticket. @deploy-bot can you queue a canary config rollback?
deploy-bot: /deploy rollback-config canary route=/chat component=kernel_selector --user=olivia --note="tighten fallback thresholds for v2 canary"
infra-monitor-bot: roll started at 1866002800. will report updated metrics in ~10m.
ryan: once rollback finishes, let's watch the model-version comparison dashboard — we should see p95 drop below threshold within 5-10 minutes if kernel is the issue.
maria: adding the new `kernel_fallback_rate` panel as a temporary top-row in the A/B dashboard. query to track: `sum(rate(kernel_selector_fallback_total[5m])) by(model_version,route) / sum(rate(runtime_tokens_count[5m])) by(model_version,route)`
olivia: thanks team. small follow-up: add a note to the rollout runbook: "when vX introduces kernel selector changes, verify kernel_fallback_rate and batcher_efficiency before promoting."
shahzad: noted. i'll also add a perf regression test to CI that runs a short long-context sampling against the canary image and fails on p95 delta > 15% vs baseline.
olivia: perfect. mark this thread resolved when infra-monitor-bot posts stable=true. :white_check_mark:
infra-monitor-bot: roll complete at 1866003200. metrics: p95 for model-v2 back to 36.0ms (under threshold), kernel_fallback_rate reduced from 0.18 -> 0.03 on canary nodes. stable=true
ryan: nice. will follow up with a short retro about kernel-selector config tests. :party_popper:
olivia: closing thread. thanks everyone.
